newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end down on correction.

text.p: China's A and B share indices closed down on Tuesday on a correction following rises in the past few sessions, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index fell 0.507 points or 0.81 percent to 62.381 points, while Shenzhen's B share index lost 3.03 points or 2.09 percent to close at 141.98 points.
Brokers said B share market sentiment was hurt by falls in the A shares due to reports that China had no immediate plans to ease credit controls.
"Rumours over the past few sessions that a further cut in bank interest rates could be announced at an ongoing national meeting of bankers had pushed up share prices," a Shenzhen trader said.
News that a major investment company had been closed for illegal and irregular practices also affected sentiment.
Shanghai's A index fell 2.38 percent or 23.054 points to 947.261 and the Shenzhen A index tumbled 8.43 points or 2.43 percent to end at 338.51 points.

"Domestic investors, who have dominated trading (on the B share markets) recently with overseas investors on the sidelines, have become cautious on uncertainties over the market," a Shanghai broker said.
In Shanghai, the B index was pushed down mainly on heavy selling in property developer Lujiazui on concerns about its 1996 results, brokers said.
Lujiazui was the day's second most heavily traded share with 2.8 million shares changing hands. It fell $0.028 or 3.39 percent to $0.796.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was again the most active share and became the second biggest loser on profit-taking, falling $0.014 or 3.93 percent to $0.342 on volume of 3.2 million shares.
In Shenzhen, Hotelier Dadonghai was the worst B share performer, declining HK$0.17 or 4.57 percent to HK$3.55 on the session's heaviest volume of 1.52 million shares on profit-taking.
On Shanghai's A share market, Shanghai-listed iron and steel producer Chengdu Gongyi was the biggest loser, falling 6.02 percent to 6.09 yuan.
In Shenzhen, Shaanxi International Trust lost the most with a fall of 7.00 percent to 10.37 yuan.
